release_commit: see GATE_IDENTITY_RECORD.json for the gated SHA
what_this_is: the four defects the review of 8b04d41 found in the funded lane, what each one actually broke, what closes it, and the counterexample that proves it. Plus three defects my own tests and the order-route census found while closing them.

defects_from_the_review.as_reported: a filled order is being confused with a closed position
what_it_broke: FILLED is absent from the outstanding-order set -- correctly, a filled order is finished -- and every read treated that one predicate as 'where the exposure is'
the one-position index released its slot the instant an entry filled
the holding disappeared from per-event and per-market collateral
all three at the point of MAXIMUM exposure, because the contracts are then actually owned
closed_by: migration 126: bettor_funded_order_is_outstanding(state) and bettor_funded_holds_inventory(residual, closed) are separate predicates; bettor_funded_position_is_open is either
the unique index bettor_funded_one_open_position is over the OPEN-POSITION subset and applies to kind='ENTRY' alone -- an exit reduces exposure and must never be refused by it
residual_qty is recomputed from the fill ledger on every write, across the whole position (the entry plus every exit naming it as parent), and never incremented
closed_at requires one of four enumerated evidenced reasons (CHECK constraint), so nothing leaves exposure by inference
exposure() reserves an outstanding order's whole clip and a terminal order's residual pro rata
counterexamples_proved: a FILLED entry holding 10 contracts reads outstanding=false, holds_inventory=true, position_open=true at the database
a second ENTRY on the same event is refused with ANOTHER_FUNDED_INTENT_IS_ALREADY_LIVE and no venue call
the rails measure the holding: per-event, per-market and correlated all read $12.40 for a second $6.20 order against $6.20 held
an invented closure reason raises; an evidenced one releases the slot
the concurrency case: the second caller's rail check passes while the first order is resting, the first order FILLS in the window, and the second caller's insert is still refused by the database

defects_from_the_review.as_reported: recovery can adopt somebody else's order -- and misses the real adapter's executions
what_it_broke: recover() took candidates[0] off a match on us_market_slug alone, so a manual desk order, a copy-lane order or another strategy's order on that market became ours -- with its fills, its cash and its place in the one-position index

recovery read st.get('fills'); pmus.order_status() has never returned that key, it returns 'executions'. So the production adapter could report a fill during downtime and recovery would ingest none of it
closed_by: correlate_venue_order: slug AND intent AND exact limit AND exact clip must all agree; exactly one survivor; an order another intent already claims is not a candidate; and a candidate created before our request left cannot be ours (120 s clock tolerance). Anything short of that stays UNRESOLVED with exposure preserved

executions_of: ONE reader for both adapter shapes -- the submit answer's raw.response.executions (lastPx/lastShares) and order_status's parsed executions (last_px/last_shares/commission_usd). The connector delegates to it, so three readers became one
a non-fill execution is reported in 'skipped' rather than dropped, and the filter is a denylist of non-fill types, because pmus's own reader says shares that executed ARE the fill
filled shares with no executions list is FILLED_SHARES_WITH_NO_EXECUTIONS -- 'the venue sent no list' is not 'the venue sent an empty one'
an adopted order is read back in the same pass, so adoption cannot leave an ACKNOWLEDGED row with no fills against a position that filled
counterexamples_proved: same market only -> refused
same market and side, different clip -> refused on quantity
same everything but the price -> refused on limit_price
the other side of our own market -> refused on order_intent
two orders both matching -> AMBIGUOUS, neither adopted
a match another intent already owns -> not a candidate
a match created before our send -> CANDIDATE_PREDATES_US
through the real pmus.open_orders with transport substituted: an unrelated same-market order is reported as an orphan and never adopted
through the real pmus.order_status: a fill during downtime is read from 'executions', written once, keyed on the venue's own execution id, and idempotent on redelivery
every timestamp shape the database and the venue can hand the clock check (datetime, naive datetime, ISO, epoch, garbage) is pinned, because a silent None there would quietly stop the check

defects_from_the_review.as_reported: funded management and P&L are not complete
what_it_broke: pnl() hardcoded realised_pnl_usd = 0.0 and check_rails() hardcoded MAX_DRAWDOWN = 0.0. 'Nothing has settled yet' described the day; a constant cannot become nonzero, so the first settlement would still have read zero in the field a loss stop reads
the scheduled path ended at entry-fill ingestion: no exit, no settlement, no recurring management
closed_by: bettor_funded_economics: one signed row per cash movement (ENTRY_COST, EXIT_PROCEEDS, FEE, SETTLEMENT, FEE_ADJUSTMENT) with a provisional flag, idempotent on event_id
realised P&L is the SUM over closed positions' events; drawdown is the worst peak-to-trough of the realised equity curve in closure order
unrealised P&L is reported UNMEASURED by name, not zero, because marking funded inventory needs a mark this lane has no source for
bettor_funded_management: exits through the same pmus.submit_fok(..., sell=True) and _exit_intent derivation the desk uses, cancels, and settlement from bettor_venue_settlement_probe
only REPORTED_SETTLEMENT and EXPLICIT_VOID close a funded position. CONVERGED_PRICE_INFERENCE is our reading of prices at 1 and 0, not a payout the venue reported
the loss stop is MAX_DRAWDOWN in the owner's effective limit set, enforced by the same check_rails every entry passes -- not a second mechanism that could disagree
FUNDED_EXIT_SUBMISSION_ENABLED is SEPARATE from the entry switch, so stopping new exposure never strands inventory; the reconciliation and settlement reads are not gated at all
the scheduled worker calls _funded_service every cycle, whether or not a candidate was admitted
counterexamples_proved: entry 10 @ 0.62 -> partial exit 4 @ 0.30 -> RESTART on a fresh connection with state read from the database alone -> final exit 6 @ 0.30 -> closed EXITED_IN_THE_MARKET with residual 0
the adapter was asked for ORDER_INTENT_SELL_LONG, derived by pmus from the BUY intent we opened with
realised P&L is the measured loss; max_drawdown equals it; a tightened MAX_DRAWDOWN rail then reads EXCEEDED and refuses the next entry
with the entry switch off, manage() still runs, opens nothing, and reports the measured drawdown
a settlement reported twice does not book the payout twice
an exit is reached while the position rule refuses another entry; it is not checked against the entry rails; it refuses without a supplied price; and it refuses a quantity larger than the residual
structurally, on the parsed module: the servicing lane has exactly two order-capable calls, submit_fok with the literal True for sell and cancel_order, and manage() calls neither

defects_from_the_review.as_reported: estimated fees are being booked as actual fees
what_it_broke: ingest_fills() always called expected_fee() and stored the result in fee_usd, and cash, P&L and the reconciliation all read that as what the venue charged
closed_by: expected_fee_usd and observed_fee_usd are separate columns with fee_state PROVISIONAL / RECONCILED / DISAGREES
the observed charge comes from the venue's own commission_usd on the execution record; None means the venue stated none, which is NOT zero
fee_usd is the number the accounting uses -- the observed charge when there is one, the expectation otherwise -- and fee_state says which
a PROVISIONAL fee inside a closed position makes the realised total explicitly incomplete rather than quietly exact
the comparison goes through the deployed calibration_fees.reconcile, in Decimal
counterexamples_proved: no stated commission -> PROVISIONAL, booked = expected, and the reason says the cash is not final
a matching commission -> RECONCILED

a commission $0.37 above the schedule -> DISAGREES; booked is the venue's number; fee_variance_usd is 0.37; cash_out_the_door uses the charge and not the estimate; the discrepancy is a row in the command centre
a closed position carrying a provisional fee reports realised_is_provisional true with a named note

defects_found_while_fixing_those.what: record_intent matched only the old index name
defects_found_while_fixing_those.how_found: the existing concurrency test in test_the_funded_book_is_durable.py
defects_found_while_fixing_those.why_it_mattered: migration 126 renamed the index, so a second concurrent submission raised UniqueViolationError out of the connector instead of returning ANOTHER_FUNDED_INTENT_IS_ALREADY_LIVE. The database still refused it -- the guarantee held -- but the caller saw an unhandled exception

the deployed module keeps money in Decimal and subtracts the observed charge directly, so a float raised. The module is right to keep money out of binary floating point; the caller had to meet it there, via str() and never Decimal(float)

defects_found_while_fixing_those.what: the book's close_position shared a name with pmus.close_position, which PLACES AN ORDER
defects_found_while_fixing_those.why_it_mattered: the census watches for two submitting entry points BY NAME. A census that cannot tell a venue submission from a bookkeeping UPDATE will one day miss a real one. Renamed mark_position_closed

defects_found_while_fixing_those.what: _recompute_residual summed only the intent's own fills
defects_found_while_fixing_those.how_found: the entry -> partial exit lifecycle test
defects_found_while_fixing_those.why_it_mattered: an exit is its own intent and its fills are written against ITS id, so the residual never moved off the full clip and the position could never close

defects_found_while_fixing_those.what: ingest_fills marked every exit FILLED on ingestion
defects_found_while_fixing_those.why_it_mattered: an exit that filled nothing read as complete, so inventory it was supposed to reduce looked serviced. Now the state follows the quantity the venue actually executed in that order's own direction

defects_found_while_fixing_those.what: migration 127: an exit commits no collateral
defects_found_while_fixing_those.how_found: the exit path could not persist its intent at all
defects_found_while_fixing_those.why_it_mattered: collateral_usd > 0 is exactly right for an ENTRY -- an order reserving nothing is one no rail measured -- and it refused the honest zero on an EXIT. The check is now kind-aware rather than relaxed

what_remains_disabled.venue_boundary: execution_gate.authorize('submit') inside pmus.submit_fok, unchanged, denies by raising
what_remains_disabled.credentials: PMUS_KEY_ID / PMUS_SECRET_KEY absent in this deployment
what_remains_disabled.deliberately_available: settlement and status reconciliation, because they submit nothing and a book that cannot be reconciled while the lane is paused is worse than one that cannot trade

venue book freshness basis and settlement compatibility: both UNRESOLVED and both still refuse entries
